note: Facts and sources behind the member descriptions in VA.json, gathered 2026-10-05. "review" holds research notes for a human check; "issues" lists open questions.

byways.name: Blue Ridge Parkway
byways.where: Rockfish Gap (milepost 0) to the North Carolina line at milepost 216.9

facts.fact: Mileposts start at zero at Rockfish Gap in Virginia; the parkway crosses into North Carolina at mile 216.9.
Virginia stops include the Humpback Rock farm buildings, the James River and Kanawha Canal locks, the Peaks of Otter and Mabry Mill, run by E.B. Mabry from 1910 to 1935.
Mabry Mill is in the parkway's Virginia Plateau district.

byways.name: Skyline Drive
byways.where: Front Royal (US 340) to Rockfish Gap (US 250 / I-64), Shenandoah National Park

facts.fact: Skyline Drive runs 105 miles along the crest of the Blue Ridge and is the only public road through Shenandoah National Park; the full length takes about three hours.
The two-lane drive has 75 overlooks over the Shenandoah Valley to the west and the Piedmont to the east; groundbreaking was in 1931.

byways.name: The Journey Through Hallowed Ground
byways.where: US 15 from the Potomac at Point of Rocks through Leesburg, Warrenton, Culpeper and Orange; SR 20, 231, 22 and 53 to Charlottesville and Scottsville

facts.fact: Designated a National Scenic Byway on October 16, 2009: 180 miles of US 15, US 15 Business and Virginia Routes 20, 231, 22 and 53.
The heritage area runs from Gettysburg to Monticello and roughly follows the Old Carolina Road; it holds nine presidential homes and sites and thirty historic main street communities.

byways.review: VDOT layer splits the Virginia part across the national line and several town Business 15 segments (Leesburg, Warrenton, Remington, Culpeper), SR 20 through Charlottesville, US 250/SR 729 near Shadwell and SR 22; all are folded into this member.

byways.name: Colonial Parkway
byways.where: Jamestown to Williamsburg to Yorktown (Colonial National Historical Park)

facts.fact: A 23-mile parkway linking Jamestown, Williamsburg and Yorktown, built in portions between 1930 and 1957 and closed to semi trucks.
Most overpasses are faced in brick in a colonial manner, and the only tunnel runs beneath Colonial Williamsburg; pull-offs near the James and York ends give views across each river.

byways.name: George Washington Memorial Parkway
byways.where: Mount Vernon through Alexandria and Arlington to I-495 near McLean

facts.fact: The parkway runs about 25 miles along the south bank of the Potomac from Mount Vernon to McLean; much of the southern section uses the old right-of-way of the Washington, Alexandria and Mount Vernon Railway.
The Mount Vernon Trail runs beside it, and Dyke Marsh, Fort Hunt and Jones Point lie along the way.
The NPS describes it as designed for recreational driving, linking more than 20 park sites including Great Falls Park and Arlington House.

byways.name: Virginia Coal Heritage Trail
byways.designation: Virginia Byway (designated by the General Assembly)
byways.where: Pocahontas to St. Paul and loops through Tazewell, Buchanan, Dickenson, Russell, Wise, Lee and Scott counties

facts.fact: The General Assembly designated the highway segments as the Virginia Coal Heritage Trail and as Virginia byways in 2007 (Chapter 531, HB 3094, approved March 19, 2007).
The trail begins at the Pocahontas Exhibition Mine and runs 325 miles through seven counties, divided into three loops.
The Pocahontas to St. Paul loop passes more than 50 coal-related sites; the Norton, Wise and Lee loop runs past old and new mining camps on curving back roads with a few hairpin turns.

byways.review: Only the segments the 2007 Act newly designated carry the General Assembly attribution in the VDOT layer; parts of the trail (Alternate 58, US 23, US 19) were already Virginia Byways as the Trail of the Lonesome Pine and are listed under that member.

byways.name: Daniel Boone Heritage Trail
byways.where: US 23 / US 58 from the Tennessee line at Weber City through Gate City and Duffield, then US 58 through Jonesville to Cumberland Gap

facts.fact: Designated March 8, 1993 as the Daniel Boone Heritage Trail on US 23 and US 58, Tennessee line near Weber City to the state line at Cumberland Gap.
West of Jonesville US 58 is named Wilderness Road and passes Wilderness Road State Park and the Wilderness Road entrance to Cumberland Gap National Historical Park.
Between Jonesville and Cumberland Gap the road runs through rolling farm country and the hamlets of Ewing and Rose Hill along Poor Valley Ridge.

byways.review: Catalog name combines this trail with the Trail of the Lonesome Pine, but the catalog line covers only this US 23 / US 58 corridor; the Lonesome Pine routes are listed separately with their own VDOT line.

byways.name: Lee's Retreat
byways.where: Five Forks (Dinwiddie) through Amelia, Sailor's Creek, Farmville and Cumberland to Appomattox

facts.fact: Designated March 20, 1995; it traces the route of the Army of Northern Virginia on April 1 to 9, 1865, from Five Forks to Appomattox Court House.
A driving tour follows the route with roadside markers; drivers tune the radio to AM 1610 for battle accounts. High Bridge is more than 2,400 feet long and 160 feet above the Appomattox River.
At Sailor's Creek on April 6, 1865, Union forces captured about 7,700 men and eight Confederate generals; Lee surrendered 72 hours later.

byways.name: Georgetown Pike
byways.where: SR 193 from SR 7 at Dranesville through Great Falls to SR 123 at Langley, Fairfax County

facts.fact: SR 193 runs 11.79 miles from Dranesville to Langley and was the first Virginia Byway, designated in 1974.
The pike was built as a stone-paved turnpike between 1813 and 1827; near Great Falls it passes so close to the river that the falls can be heard from the road.
Designated June 20, 1974; the CTB minutes record it as leading to Great Falls Park.

byways.name: Trail of the Lonesome Pine
byways.where: US 19 from Bluefield through Tazewell to Lebanon, SR 71, US Alternate 58 through St. Paul, Norton and Big Stone Gap to Jonesville, SR 70, US 23 north to Pound Gap, SR 160 from Appalachia to Black Mountain

facts.fact: Designated March 8, 1993 on US 19, SR 71, US Alternate 58, SR 70, US 23 and SR 160, with business routes through Tazewell, Lebanon, Norton, Big Stone Gap, Wise and Pound.
US 19 east of Lebanon is named the Trail of the Lonesome Pine; with US 460 it follows the Clinch River and the Clinch Valley rail line through Pounding Mill to Tazewell.
Big Stone Gap, at the junction of US 23 and Alternate 58, has the John Fox Jr. House, the June Tolliver House and Southwest Virginia Museum Historical State Park.

byways.review: No separate catalog line; draw from the VDOT layer (gisWhere). Overlaps the Virginia Coal Heritage Trail on Alternate 58 and US 23.

byways.name: Fairfax County byways
byways.where: Clifton-area roads (Clifton, Yates Ford, Henderson, Popes Head, Newman, Fairfax Station, Compton, Pleasant Valley), Hunter Mill Road, Colvin Run Road, Old Reston Avenue and Old Colchester Road

facts.fact: Clifton grew around an 1868 railroad depot; to protect Bull Run and the Occoquan Reservoir, parcels around it are limited to one building per five acres, keeping the land far less built up than most of Northern Virginia.
Colvin Run Mill, built about 1811, is the only working 19th-century water-powered mill left in the Washington area.

Clifton Road (1994), Yates Ford Road (1997), Henderson Road (2001), Pleasant Valley and Fairfax Station roads (2004), Newman Road (2008), Popes Head Road (2009) and Compton Road (2011) were designated around Clifton; Hunter Mill Road in 2002 and Colvin Run Road, a former line of SR 7, in 2000.

byways.review: Georgetown Pike (SR 193) is listed separately. Union Mill Road (SR 659, 1999) and the SR 825 part of Old Colchester Road are listed but absent from the VDOT layer.

byways.name: Prince William County byways
byways.where: Waterfall Road (SR 601), Antioch Road (SR 681), John Marshall Highway (SR 55) to the Fauquier line; Aden Road (SR 646), Bristow Road and Joplin Road (SR 619) to I-95

facts.fact: The CTB designated these six roads, 39.4 miles in all, on December 7, 2016 at the request of the Prince William County Board of Supervisors, the county's first Virginia Byways.
The corridors pass the Brentsville Historic District, Prince William Forest Park, the Broad Run/Little Georgetown rural historic district, Chapman's Mill (Beverly Mill) and several battlefields.
Brentsville was the Prince William County seat from 1820 to 1894.
Waterfall Road and John Marshall Highway connect with existing Virginia Byways in Fauquier County, in the county's Rural Crescent.

byways.review: The Wikipedia list dates Aden Road to July 11, 2017; the CTB resolution and the VDOT layer give December 7, 2016.

byways.name: Loudoun County byways
byways.where: Snickersville Turnpike (SR 734); SR 9 (Charles Town Pike) to Keyes Gap; roads around Waterford, Hillsboro, Lovettsville and Taylorstown; Harpers Ferry Road; Business 7 and Dry Mill Road from Hamilton to Leesburg

facts.fact: Snickersville Turnpike (SR 734) between Aldie and Bluemont is a rural Virginia Byway with the roughly 180-year-old Hibbs Bridge over Beaverdam Creek; it follows part of one of the first turnpike roads in the country.
Waterford, settled around 1733 by the Quaker Amos Janney around his mills on Catoctin Creek, was designated a National Historic Landmark District in 1970.
SR 9 descends from Keyes Gap on the Blue Ridge into the narrow valley called Between the Hills and passes through Hillsboro Gap along the North Fork of Catoctin Creek.

byways.review: SR 719 (Stoney Point Road, 1988) is listed but absent from the VDOT layer; Business US 15 in Leesburg is folded into the Journey Through Hallowed Ground member.

byways.name: Fauquier County byways
byways.where: SR 55 from Linden to Thoroughfare Gap; US 17 from Paris to I-66; Leeds Manor, Crest Hill, Hume, Rectortown, Atoka, Zulla and Delaplane Grade roads; Rappahannock River roads by Remington; Catlett and Elk Run roads

facts.fact: Most Fauquier byways, including SR 55 from Linden to Thoroughfare Gap and Leeds Manor Road from Paris to Waterloo, were designated together on September 19, 1996; the Sumerduck and Freemans Ford roads parallel the Rappahannock River.
SR 55 crosses the Blue Ridge at Manassas Gap near Linden, passes Oak Hill, John Marshall's country estate, and runs through Marshall and The Plains to Thoroughfare Gap in the Bull Run Mountains.
US 17 runs as Winchester Road through Delaplane, past the entrance to Sky Meadows State Park, to Paris.

byways.review: Not in the VDOT layer although listed from CTB minutes: SR 602 (Rogues Road), SR 623 (Rokeby Road) and SR 733/738 (Wilson Road). SR 601 from The Plains to the Prince William line (dated July 28, 2016 in the layer) is included.

byways.name: Routes 245 and 626, Old Tavern to Middleburg, with Springs Road
byways.where: SR 245 (Old Tavern Road) from US 17 to The Plains; SR 626 (Halfway Road) to Middleburg; SR 802 (Springs Road) from Jeffersonton to Warrenton

facts.fact: SR 245 (Old Tavern Road) runs from US 17 at Old Tavern through farmland, crossing Piney Branch of Broad Run, into The Plains.
SR 245 with SR 626 (Halfway Road) to Middleburg, a former alignment of US 15, and SR 802 (Springs Road) to Warrenton were designated September 15, 1983.

byways.name: Clarke County byways
byways.where: SR 255 and SR 723 through Millwood and Boyce; White Post, Berrys Ferry and Bordens Spring roads; River Road (SR 606), Howellsville Road, Blue Ridge Mountain Road (SR 601) along the crest, and other county roads

facts.fact: Millwood holds many of Clarke County's historic sites, including the Burwell-Morgan Mill (1785), Carter Hall (1792), Long Branch (1811) and Old Chapel (1790).
The Burwell-Morgan Mill was built about 1785 by Daniel Morgan and Nathaniel Burwell, ran until the 1950s and is now a museum.
White Post takes its name from a post that, by tradition, George Washington set to guide travelers to Lord Fairfax's Greenway Court.
Most of the Clarke roads were designated May 17, 1990; SR 601 (Blue Ridge Mountain Road) runs atop the Blue Ridge past Mount Weather, and Howellsville Road parallels the Shenandoah River.

byways.name: Route 55, Star Tannery to Front Royal
byways.where: SR 55 from Star Tannery (Frederick Co.) to Strasburg and on to Front Royal (Frederick, Shenandoah, Warren)

facts.fact: From Great North Mountain SR 55 descends through George Washington National Forest to Star Tannery, passes Lebanon Church to Strasburg, and crosses the North Fork Shenandoah River below Signal Knob, the north end of Massanutten Mountain.
It reaches Front Royal at Riverton, where the North and South forks join to form the Shenandoah.
Designated June 12, 1997, from the Frederick County line at Star Tannery to Front Royal.

byways.name: Back Road, Middle Road and Star Tannery Road (Shenandoah and Frederick)
byways.where: SR 623 (Back Road) from SR 55 near Lebanon Church to SR 42; SR 614 (Middle Road) to US 11 at Bowmans Crossing; SR 600 and SR 604 from Maurertown over Fetzer Gap to Star Tannery; SR 661 Redbud Road (Frederick)

facts.fact: Designated June 21, 2001: Back Road from SR 55 to Columbia Furnace and Forestville, Middle Road from Forestville to Bowmans Crossing, and SR 600 with SR 604 (Star Tannery Road) from US 11 near Maurertown through Fetzer Gap to Star Tannery.
Star Tannery lies on Star Tannery Road off SR 55 along Cedar Creek, on the Shenandoah County line.
Woodstock, the Shenandoah county seat, lies along the Seven Bends of the North Fork of the Shenandoah River.

byways.name: Shenandoah County byways
byways.where: US 11 (Old Valley Pike) from New Market to Strasburg; SR 263 (Orkney Grade); SR 675 and SR 717 from Camp Roosevelt through Edinburg Gap to Basye; SR 42 and SR 767 to Quicksburg

facts.fact: US 11 from New Market to Strasburg (Old Valley Pike), SR 263 (Orkney Grade), SR 675 and 717 past Columbia Furnace and Edinburg Gap, and SR 42 with SR 767 were all designated June 21, 2001.
SR 263 runs from Shrine Mont at Orkney Springs, home of the Shenandoah Valley Music Festival, down a narrow valley past Bryce Resort to Mount Jackson.
Orkney Springs grew around mineral springs; its hotels consolidated into the Orkney Springs Hotel, listed on the National Register in 1976.
Camp Roosevelt Recreation Area lies in Fort Valley, the valley within a valley inside Massanutten Mountain.

byways.name: Page County byways
byways.where: US 211 from New Market Gap through Luray to Thornton Gap; US 340 from Overall to the Rockingham line; SR 675, SR 615, SR 616, SR 636 and SR 650 along the South Fork (Page)

facts.fact: US 211 climbs Massanutten Mountain to New Market Gap, crosses the South Fork Shenandoah River at Whitehouse Landing, passes Luray Caverns and climbs the Blue Ridge to Thornton Gap and Skyline Drive.
In the Page Valley, between the Blue Ridge and Massanutten Mountain, US 340 runs through the Shenandoah historic district and Stanley to Luray and north past Rileyville to Overall.
SR 615 (Egypt Bend Road) parallels the Shenandoah River, and SR 675 runs from Luray toward Camp Roosevelt Recreation Area (2005); US 211 and the US 340 river roads followed in 2008.

byways.name: US 340, Front Royal to Overall
byways.where: US 340 (Stonewall Jackson Highway) from Skyline Drive at Front Royal to the Page County line at Overall (Warren)

facts.fact: South of Front Royal US 340 runs through Karo, Limeton and Bentonville, site of Shenandoah River State Park, and crosses Overall Run on the Overall Bridge, a Pratt deck arch truss beside the railroad bridge.
Designated February 15, 2006; it parallels the South Fork Shenandoah River.

byways.name: Rappahannock County byways (Flint Hill and Ben Venue)
byways.where: SR 628, 606, 641 and 647 (Fodderstack and Crest Hill roads) from Washington through Flint Hill to the Fauquier line; SR 729 (Ben Venue Road and Richmond Road)

facts.fact: SR 628, 606, 641 (Fodderstack Road) and 647 (Crest Hill Road) from Washington by Flint Hill to the Rappahannock River were designated May 17, 1990; SR 729 Ben Venue Road, part of former SR 242, in 2009.
Washington, known as Little Washington, sits in the eastern foothills of the Blue Ridge near Shenandoah National Park, and the whole town is a historic district.
Ben Venue, near Washington, is a brick farmhouse of 1844 to 1846 whose grounds keep three brick slave cabins, a kitchen and a smokehouse.

byways.name: US 522, Culpeper to Chester Gap
byways.where: US 522 from US 15 Business in Culpeper through Sperryville, Washington and Flint Hill to SR 635 near Chester Gap (Culpeper, Rappahannock)

facts.fact: From Culpeper, US 522 runs as Sperryville Pike into the Blue Ridge foothills past Griffinsburg and the village of Boston, through the gap between Butler and Bessie Bell mountains to Woodville and the Sperryville historic district.
North of Washington it becomes Zachary Taylor Highway through Flint Hill and climbs to Chester Gap, where it crosses the Appalachian Trail near the headwaters of the Rappahannock.
Designated April 20, 2000 from US 15 Business in Culpeper to SR 635 near Chester Gap.

byways.name: Route 231 (Blue Ridge Turnpike and F.T. Valley Road)
byways.where: SR 231 from Gordonsville through Somerset and Madison to US 522 near Sperryville, with SR 687 at Madison (Orange, Madison, Rappahannock)

facts.fact: North of Gordonsville SR 231 follows Blue Ridge Turnpike over the Southwest Mountains past Frascati plantation, crosses the Rapidan, and runs through Madison.
North of the Robinson River it follows F.T. Valley Road, named for Francis Thornton, through the foothills past Etlan, directly east of Old Rag Mountain, to Sperryville.
Designated August 18, 1988; the part south of SR 20 is now on the Journey Through Hallowed Ground.

byways.name: Route 615 (Rapidan Road), Orange to Rapidan
byways.where: SR 615 from SR 20 Business in Orange to SR 614 at Rapidan (Orange, Culpeper)

facts.fact: Designated September 15, 1999 from Orange to Rapidan.
Rapidan straddles the Rapidan River around the old Waugh's Ford mill site; the Orange and Alexandria Railroad came through in 1854, and milling lasted into the mid-twentieth century.

byways.name: Route 613, Green Springs
byways.where: SR 613 from US 250 near Zion Crossroads to US 522 / SR 208 at Wares Crossroads (Louisa)

facts.fact: Green Springs, bounded partly by SR 613, became the first rural National Historic Landmark district: 14,000 acres of manor houses in an intact farm landscape, named for a spring Jefferson noted.
Designated March 18, 2004, with Green Springs Historic District as its destination.

byways.name: Albemarle County byways (Garth Road and Thomas Jefferson Parkway)
byways.where: SR 601, SR 676 and SR 614 (Garth Road) from Charlottesville through Owensville to White Hall; SR 53 (Thomas Jefferson Parkway) from SR 20 to the Fluvanna line

facts.fact: SR 601, SR 676 and SR 614 (Garth Road) from US 29/250 to White Hall were designated July 16, 1987 and are part of U.S. Bike Route 76; SR 53 (Thomas Jefferson Parkway) was added November 20, 2008, with Monticello as its destination.
SR 53 climbs Carters Mountain past Michie Tavern and winds over the summit between Monticello and Montalto, then descends to Simeon, where a road leads to James Monroe's Ashlawn-Highland.
White Hall was earlier known as Maupin's Tavern and Shumate's Tavern, among other names, until 1835.

byways.review: SR 53 west of SR 729 is also part of the Journey Through Hallowed Ground.

byways.name: Route 6 and US 250 west of Charlottesville
byways.where: SR 6 / SR 151 from Scottsville to Afton; US 250 from Charlottesville to Rockfish Gap (Albemarle and Nelson)

facts.fact: SR 6 runs from Scottsville through Esmont and Faber, follows the Rockfish River and then the Rockfish Valley, and climbs Afton Mountain to US 250 about a mile east of Rockfish Gap.
US 250 here follows roughly the 18th-century Three Notch'd Road and climbs the Blue Ridge to Rockfish Gap as the Rockfish Gap Turnpike.
SR 6 was designated August 19, 1976 and US 250 December 17, 1981.

byways.name: Route 6 (River Road), Scottsville to Henrico
byways.where: SR 6 from Scottsville through Fluvanna and Goochland to SR 650 and River Road into Henrico

facts.fact: East of Scottsville SR 6 runs as River Road through Fork Union, home of Fork Union Military Academy, and the river town of Columbia before reaching Goochland.
From Scottsville to Richmond the highway parallels the James River.
Designated January 15, 1987 from Scottsville to SR 150 near Tuckahoe, with River Road (SR 650) in Goochland.

byways.name: Nelson County byways (Crabtree Falls Highway)
byways.where: SR 56 from Tye River Gap to Roseland; SR 664 (Beech Grove Road) to Reeds Gap; SR 617 (Rockfish River Road) and SR 800 to Schuyler

facts.fact: East of Tye River Gap SR 56 becomes Crabtree Falls Highway, descending through Montebello and along the South Fork of the Tye past Crabtree Falls, then by the Tyro Mill and Massies Mill to Roseland.
SR 664 (Beech Grove Road) climbs from near Wintergreen to the Blue Ridge Parkway at Reeds Gap (2005); SR 617 and SR 800 run along the Rockfish River to Schuyler (2011).

byways.name: US 11 and Route 56 (Tye River Turnpike), Augusta and Rockbridge
byways.where: US 11 from Lexington to SR 130 at Natural Bridge; SR 56 from US 11 at Steeles Tavern to the Blue Ridge Parkway at Tye River Gap

facts.fact: SR 56 begins at Steeles Tavern near the historic Cyrus McCormick Farm and, as Tye River Turnpike, passes under the railroad at Vesuvius and climbs beside Little Marys Creek to the Parkway at Tye River Gap.
Much of US 11 roughly follows the Great Wagon Road, the colonial road along the Appalachians.
US 11 from Lexington to Natural Bridge and SR 56 (Tye River Turnpike) were designated December 18, 1997.

byways.name: Route 39 and Rockbridge County byways (Goshen Pass)
byways.where: SR 39 from Lexington through Goshen Pass and Warm Springs to the West Virginia line; SR 252 and SR 606 to Steeles Tavern; SR 663 River Road (Rockbridge and Bath)

facts.fact: All of SR 39 is a Virginia Byway; it runs from East Lexington through Goshen Pass, a gorge cut by the Maury River, to Warm Springs and the West Virginia line at Ryder Gap.
In Bath County the road passes the Jefferson Pools at Warm Springs and follows the Cowpasture River to Millboro Springs.
Goshen Pass has a memorial to Matthew Fontaine Maury with an anchor and chain set above the river.

byways.name: Route 130, Natural Bridge to Elon
byways.where: SR 130 from US 11 at Natural Bridge through Glasgow and the James River gorge to US 29 Business near Madison Heights

facts.fact: SR 130 begins beside the Natural Bridge Hotel, passes through Glasgow and, with US 501, follows the James River through its gorge in the Blue Ridge.
East of the gorge it crosses the Pedlar River and passes a gap in Tobacco Row Mountain to the hamlet of Elon.
Designated January 15, 1987, with the James River gorge and Natural Bridge listed as destinations.

byways.name: Route 629 to Douthat State Park
byways.where: SR 629 (Douthat State Park Road) from I-64 at Cliftondale Park to SR 39 near Bath Alum (Alleghany, Bath)

facts.fact: Douthat State Park, 4,545 acres with a 50-acre lake in the Allegheny Mountains, is one of Virginia's six original state parks, built by the Civilian Conservation Corps between 1933 and 1942.
Designated March 2, 1997.

byways.name: Routes 311, 42, 43 and 159 in the Alleghany Highlands
byways.where: SR 311 from Hanging Rock (Roanoke Co.) through Catawba, New Castle and Paint Bank to West Virginia; SR 42 Newport to New Castle; SR 615 and SR 43 to the Parkway at Bearwallow Gap; SR 159; SR 621 and SR 616 to Low Moor

facts.fact: SR 311 climbs Catawba Mountain across the Appalachian Trail, enters Jefferson National Forest at McAfee Gap, and follows Craig Creek to New Castle and on to Paint Bank.
SR 42 in Craig County follows Meadow Creek past Meadow Creek Falls and drops from 2,570 feet at Looney to 1,310 feet at New Castle.
The northern section of SR 43 follows the James River through a narrow valley on Narrow Passage Road between Buchanan and Eagle Rock.
These routes were designated together on December 20, 1990.

byways.name: Route 785, Catawba Valley
byways.where: SR 785 from Lusters Gate (Montgomery Co.) to SR 311 near Catawba (Roanoke Co.)

facts.fact: Designated May 15, 1986; part of U.S. Bike Route 76 and former SR 114.
At Catawba, SR 779 and SR 785 form the main road along the valley of Catawba Creek, just over Catawba Mountain from the Roanoke Valley.
Catawba is a rural enclave of farms in the Catawba Valley between Catawba Mountain and the Craig County line; Catawba Hospital traces back to an 1857 sulphur spring resort.

byways.name: Whistle Stop Byway
byways.where: SR 635 (Big Stony Creek Road) from US 460 near Pembroke to West Virginia; SR 600 (Waiteville Road) from West Virginia to SR 311 at Paint Bank (Giles, Craig)

facts.fact: Designated September 15, 2010 as the Whistle Stop Byway; it mostly follows the former Big Stony Railway of the Norfolk and Western, and the two Virginia pieces are linked through Monroe County, West Virginia.
Pembroke, near the southern end, was settled in the mid-1750s along the New River.
Paint Bank, where the byway meets SR 311, lies between Potts Mountain and Peters Mountain and is named for the iron ochre and red clay once taken from the banks of Potts Creek.

byways.name: Routes 43 and 24, Altavista to the Peaks of Otter
byways.where: SR 43 from Altavista through Leesville and Bedford to the Blue Ridge Parkway at Peaks of Otter; SR 24 from US 29 to SR 43 at Gillespie (Campbell and Bedford)

facts.fact: SR 43 runs north from Altavista along the Roanoke River above Leesville Lake, through the town of Bedford and up to the Blue Ridge Parkway at Peaks of Otter; north of SR 24 the road is named Virginia Byway.
SR 24 (Colonial Highway) was added October 17, 2012, passing Evington and the Flat Creek Rural Historic District.

byways.name: Franklin County roads to the Parkway
byways.where: SR 602 (Callaway Road) and SR 623 from Adney Gap through Callaway and Ferrum to the Patrick line near Fairy Stone State Park; SR 640 and SR 748 from the Parkway to SR 40 (Franklin, Floyd)

facts.fact: Designated November 19, 1998: SR 602 and SR 623 through Callaway and Ferrum to the Patrick County line near Fairy Stone State Park, and SR 640 (Five Mile Mountain Road) from the Blue Ridge Parkway toward Rocky Mount.
Fairy Stone State Park is named for the cross-shaped staurolite stones found nearby and is one of six original state parks opened June 15, 1936.

byways.name: US 58 (J.E.B. Stuart Highway), Meadows of Dan to Stuart
byways.where: US 58 from SR 8 north of Stuart to the Blue Ridge Parkway at Meadows of Dan (Patrick)

facts.fact: Designated May 19, 2005: US 58 and Business 58 (J.E.B. Stuart Highway) from SR 8 north of Stuart to the Blue Ridge Parkway at Meadows of Dan.
Meadows of Dan, where the Parkway crosses US 58 at milepost 178, has country shops and older houses and is named for the meadows along the Dan River; it lies about 14 miles northwest of Stuart.
Between Meadows of Dan and Martinsville US 58 winds down off the Blue Ridge, and much of the highway in this region has hairpin turns and steep grades.

byways.review: The VDOT layer draws this designation (LAD_SOURCE Patrick County) along US 58 all the way from Damascus through Independence, Galax and Hillsville, about 120 route miles, although its own description and LAD_SCEN_1 (12) say SR 8 to the Parkway. gisWhere below is restricted to RTE_FROM_M >= 221 (route miles 221.9 to 235.5, 40 rows), which matches the described section; verify before drawing.

byways.name: Routes 91, 58, 603 and 600 around Damascus and Whitetop
byways.where: SR 91 from Glade Spring through Damascus to Tennessee; US 58 Damascus to Konnarock; SR 603 Konnarock to Troutdale; SR 600 Whitetop Road to North Carolina (Washington, Smyth, Grayson)

facts.fact: SR 91 runs from Glade Spring past the village of Lodi and its Holston River crossings to Damascus, then follows Laurel Creek through the Iron Mountains to Tennessee, crossing the Virginia Creeper Trail.

US 58 (J.E.B. Stuart Highway) with SR 603 from Laureldale to Troutdale, and SR 600 (Whitetop Road) past Elk Garden and Whitetop Mountain to the North Carolina line, were designated September 21, 2000.

byways.review: Overlaps the Mount Rogers National Forest Scenic Byway (US 58 and SR 603), listed under the Forest Service program.

byways.name: Wythe County byways
byways.where: US 52, SR 121 and SR 610 from Poplar Camp by Max Meadows toward Wytheville; SR 619 (Austinville Road) and SR 749, SR 90 and SR 680 from Laswell by Austinville, Speedwell and Rural Retreat to Favonia

facts.fact: Designated March 21, 2002: US 52 (Fort Chiswell Road), SR 121 (Max Meadows Road) and SR 610 (Peppers Ferry Road) by Max Meadows, and SR 619, 749, 90 and 680 through Rural Retreat and Speedwell country.
Austinville, on the New River, is the birthplace of Stephen F. Austin; New River Trail State Park runs through it and Shot Tower Historical State Park is nearby.
The Jackson Ferry Shot Tower stands along the New River and was used for many years to make ammunition.

byways.name: US 52 and Big Walker Mountain roads (Bland and Wythe)
byways.where: US 52 (Scenic Highway) and SR 717 between I-77 near Bland and I-77 near Carnot; SR 617 (Waddletown Road) south of Bland

facts.fact: US 52 (Scenic Highway / Stony Fork Road) with SR 717, from I-77 near Bland to I-77 near Carnot, and SR 617 were designated September 17, 1992.
The US 52 section climbs to Big Walker Lookout, a 100-foot tower with a 360-degree view; Bland, east of the route, offers vistas and historic landmarks.
Bland, the county seat of Bland County, was originally known as Bland Court House.

byways.review: These roads are also the Big Walker Mountain National Forest Scenic Byway, listed under the Forest Service program.

byways.name: Route 16, Sugar Grove to Tazewell
byways.where: SR 16 from Dickey Gap / Sugar Grove through Marion to US 19-460 at Pisgah (Smyth and Tazewell)

facts.fact: From Sugar Grove SR 16 crosses Brushy Mountain and the Appalachian Trail, enters Marion, and passes Hungry Mother Lake and Hungry Mother State Park before crossing Walker Mountain.
The 32 miles between Marion and Tazewell, known as the Back of the Dragon, cross Brushy and Clinch mountains with twisting descents and a hairpin into Thompson Valley.
Designated January 20, 2000 from SR 650 at Dickey Gap to US 19/460 at Pisgah.

byways.name: Burke's Garden roads
byways.where: SR 623 (Burkes Garden Road) from SR 61 at Gratton into Burke's Garden, with SR 667, 727, 625 and 666 around the valley (Tazewell)

facts.fact: Burke's Garden is an oval upland valley about 8.5 miles long and 4 miles wide, ringed by Garden Mountain, at around 3,000 feet the second highest valley in Virginia.
Though it looks like a crater on maps, it is an eroded dome of limestone inside sandstone ridges, known for its fertile land.
SR 623 was designated June 22, 1979; the loop roads inside the valley on February 20, 1992.

byways.name: Route 640, St. Paul to Wardell
byways.designation: Virginia Byway (designated by the General Assembly)
byways.where: SR 640 (River Road, Reeds Valley Road, Middle Valley Road and others) from St. Paul to SR 770 near Wardell (Russell)

facts.fact: Designated March 5, 1996 by the General Assembly (Acts chapter 714): SR 640 from St. Paul to SR 770 near Wardell under the names River Road, Reeds Valley Road, Middle Valley Road, Long Hollow Road, River Mountain Road and Clifton Farm Road; part of the Heart of Appalachia Bike Route.
St. Paul lies in the mountains along the Clinch River and began as a French Huguenot settlement overlooking the river in 1791.

byways.name: Dickenson County, Routes 631 and 611
byways.where: SR 631 (Brush Creek Road) from Clintwood and SR 611 (South of the Mountain, Blowing Rock and Bartlick roads) to SR 80 near Haysi

facts.fact: Designated November 19, 2009: SR 631 from SR 83 in Clintwood and SR 611 through Isom, Blowing Rock and Bartlick to SR 80 near Haysi.
Clintwood, the Dickenson County seat, was founded in 1829 and first called Holly Creek after the stream through town.

byways.name: Halifax County byways
byways.where: SR 344 from Staunton River State Park through Scottsburg and SR 360 through Halifax to the Pittsylvania line; SR 654 and SR 659 (River Road) to Brooklyn

facts.fact: SR 344 runs from Staunton River State Park, at the meeting of the Roanoke (Staunton) and Dan rivers, through Scottsburg to SR 360.
SR 360 is the old alignment of US 360; it crosses the Banister River and passes the Halifax County courthouse in the town of Halifax before heading west as Mountain Road.
SR 344 and SR 360 were designated July 20, 2006; SR 654 (Greens Folly Road) and SR 659 (River Road) on July 20, 1989.

byways.name: Route 47, South Hill to Pamplin
byways.where: SR 47 from South Hill through Chase City, Drakes Branch and Charlotte Court House to Pamplin (Mecklenburg, Charlotte, Prince Edward, Appomattox)

facts.fact: The entire length of SR 47 is a Virginia Byway; it runs along the divide between the Meherrin and Roanoke rivers through North View, Wightman and Drapersville to Chase City.
It continues through Craftons Gate, Drakes Branch and the county seat of Charlotte Court House, and follows the Charlotte and Prince Edward county line for a stretch.
Designated January 18, 2006.

byways.name: Charlotte and Campbell County roads (Route 40 to Red Hill)
byways.where: SR 40 from Charlotte Court House through Phenix with SR 600 and SR 619 to Red Hill; SR 637, 612, 641 and 607 (River Road) from Drakes Branch to Randolph

facts.fact: Designated July 20, 2006: SR 40 and county roads from Charlotte Court House toward the Patrick Henry National Memorial, and a run of county roads from Drakes Branch to Randolph ending on River Road.
Patrick Henry gave his last political speech at Charlotte Courthouse in March 1799; the town keeps a courthouse designed by Thomas Jefferson.
Red Hill, near Brookneal on the Staunton River, was Patrick Henry's last home and is his burial place.

byways.name: Route 696 (Green Bay Road), Prince Edward County
byways.where: SR 696 from US 360 at Green Bay to US 460 near Farmville (Prince Edward)

facts.fact: SR 696 (Green Bay Road), a former SR 135, runs from US 360 at Green Bay to US 460 near Farmville; it is on the VDOT byways map though its designation date is uncertain.
VDOT's layer records it as running from Route 360 west of Green Bay to Route 460 east of Farmville, at the request of Prince Edward County.

byways.name: Robinson Ferry and Gasburg roads, Brunswick County
byways.where: SR 903 (Hendricks Mill Road) and SR 626 (Robinson Ferry Road / Gasburg Road) from the Mecklenburg line near Joyceville to SR 46 at Bowens Corner (Brunswick)

facts.fact: Designated June 17, 2004: SR 903 (Hendricks Mill Road) and SR 626 (Robinson Ferry Road / Gasburg Road) from the Mecklenburg County line near Joyceville to SR 46 at Bowens Corner.
Gasburg, on the route, is a small rural community of about 400 people.

byways.review: The SR 903 (Hendricks Mill Road) part is not in the VDOT layer; only SR 626 is drawn.

byways.name: Huguenot Trail and Old River Trail, west of Richmond
byways.where: SR 673 (Old Gun Road) and SR 711 (Robious Road / Huguenot Trail) from Richmond to Jefferson; SR 617 (Old River Trail) from Jefferson to US 522 at Michaux (Chesterfield, Powhatan, Richmond)

facts.fact: Designated February 15, 1990: Old Gun Road and Robious Road / Huguenot Trail from SR 147 in Richmond to US 522 at Jefferson, and Old River Trail (SR 617) in Powhatan from near Jefferson to Michaux.
VDOT describes the Richmond piece as running from Old Gun Road at the west city limits to Route 147.

byways.name: Route 5 (John Tyler Highway)
byways.where: SR 5 from the Richmond city line through Henrico and Charles City counties to Williamsburg

facts.fact: SR 5 follows the north bank of the James along older colonial roads and crosses the Chickahominy on the bridge that replaced Barrett's Ferry; the Virginia Capital Trail runs beside it.
James River plantations along the route include Shirley, Berkeley, Westover, Evelynton and Sherwood Forest.
Designated August 21, 1975 between Richmond and Williamsburg.

byways.name: New Kent County byways
byways.where: SR 249 (New Kent Highway) from Talleysville to Angelview Church; SR 609 Old Church Road; SR 608 Old River Road and SR 606 by Tunstall Station

facts.fact: SR 249 (New Kent Highway), the old line of SR 33, runs through Talleysville and Carps Corner to the county seat of New Kent and on to Angelview Church.
SR 249 with SR 609 (Old Church Road / Talleysville Road) and SR 608 (Old River Road) with SR 606 past Tunstall Station were designated May 15, 2003.

byways.name: Greensprings Road and Jamestown Festival Parkway
byways.where: SR 614 (Centerville and Greensprings roads) from near Green Spring Plantation and SR 359 to the Colonial Parkway near Jamestown (James City)

facts.fact: Designated December 18, 1997: SR 614 from near Green Spring Plantation and SR 359 (Jamestown Festival Parkway) to the Colonial Parkway near Jamestown.
Green Spring Plantation, about five miles west of Williamsburg, was the 17th-century plantation of Governor Sir William Berkeley.
Jamestown Settlement began as Jamestown Festival Park in 1957 and has a recreated James Fort, a Powhatan town and replicas of the Susan Constant, Godspeed and Discovery.

byways.name: Caroline County, Routes 606 and 721
byways.where: SR 606 (Stonewall Jackson Road) from SR 2 at Locks Corner; SR 721 (Newtown and Sparta roads) from US 360 at St. Stephens Church to US 301

facts.fact: SR 606 (Stonewall Jackson Road) and SR 607 (Guinea Station Road) were designated March 21, 2002, with the Stonewall Jackson death site as destination.
SR 721 (Newtown Road / Sparta Road), the former extension of SR 14, was designated June 20, 2002.
SR 721 is the old route of SR 14, continuing northwest from St. Stephens Church toward Bowling Green.

byways.name: US 17 (Tidewater Trail), Tappahannock to Spotsylvania County
byways.where: US 17 from the north limits of Tappahannock through Essex and Caroline to the Spotsylvania County line

facts.fact: North of Tappahannock US 17 runs as Tidewater Trail through Caret, Champlain, Chance and Loretto, crosses Portobogo Creek into Caroline County and passes the town of Port Royal.
Tappahannock, on the Rappahannock River, is the oldest town in Essex County and its county seat; John Smith landed there in 1608.
Designated April 12, 2004; the road parallels the Rappahannock River.

byways.name: Spotsylvania County byways
byways.where: SR 618 (River Road) from SR 3 at Chancellorsville to SR 639 near Fredericksburg; SR 607 (Guinea Station Road) to US 1 near Massaponax

facts.fact: SR 618 (River Road) runs from SR 3 at Chancellorsville toward Fredericksburg (1997); SR 607 continues the Guinea Station road from the Stonewall Jackson death site to US 1 (2002).
Chancellorsville, fought May 1 to 3, 1863, is one of the four battles commemorated by Fredericksburg and Spotsylvania National Military Park.

byways.name: Route 218, King George County
byways.where: SR 218 from Passapatanzy to SR 206 at Berthaville, and from US 301 near Owens to SR 205 at Tetotum

facts.fact: In King George County SR 218 (Caledon Road) winds through forest past Passapatanzy, Mustoe, Goby and Osso, near roads to the Potomac beach communities.
It skirts Caledon Natural Area, a National Natural Landmark with old-growth forest known as a haven for bald eagles.
Designated March 20, 1997 in two pieces.

byways.name: Westmoreland County byways
byways.where: SR 3 from Oak Grove to Montross, SR 622 to Currioman Landing, SR 204 to Popes Creek, SR 347 to Westmoreland State Park, SR 214 and SR 609 to Stratford Hall

facts.fact: SR 3 (Kings Highway) passes the historic Westmoreland County Courthouse in Montross, and from it SR 347 leads into Westmoreland State Park and SR 204 to the George Washington Birthplace National Monument.
VDOT describes SR 204 and SR 347 as running from Route 3 to the Potomac River, and SR 622 from Montross to the Potomac at Currioman Landing on Currioman Bay.
Designated August 15, 2002: SR 3 and SR 622 from Oak Grove to Currioman Landing, SR 204 (Popes Creek Road), SR 347 (State Park Road), and SR 214 with SR 609 (Stratford Hall Road).

byways.name: Northumberland County byways
byways.where: Necks and points of the lower county: SR 679, Balls Neck Road to Hughlett Point, Bluff Point and Ditchley roads, the Hull Neck to Reedville route via the Sunnybank ferry (SR 644), Fleeton Road

facts.fact: A 1992 route from US 360 near Avalon to Reedville was laid out to run as close to the Potomac as possible, crossing by the Sunny Bank Ferry; other byways run down Bluff Point Neck, Balls Neck and to Fleeton.
VDOT describes SR 644 as crossing the Little Wicomico River by means of the Sunnybank Ferry.
Reedville, on Cockrell's Creek off the Chesapeake, is the home port of the menhaden fishery and has a Millionaire's Row of Victorian mansions.
Hughlett Point Natural Area Preserve protects 204 acres of beaches, dunes, marsh and upland forest and is a staging area for migrating birds.

byways.name: Lancaster County byways
byways.where: SR 354 (River Road) from Litwalton to Ottoman, SR 604 by the Merry Point ferry to Lancaster, SR 3 to White Stone, SR 200 through Irvington and Kilmarnock, SR 614 (Devils Bottom Road)

facts.fact: SR 354 (River Road) runs down the neck between the Rappahannock and the Western Branch of the Corrotoman past Somers, near Belle Isle State Park, to Ottoman, site of a free ferry across the Western Branch.
SR 200 links White Stone, Irvington and Kilmarnock and passes historic Christ Church at Pitmans Corner.
Designated April 16, 1998 as a loop through White Stone that crosses itself in Kilmarnock, listing Merry Point Ferry among its destinations.

byways.name: Route 14 (The Trail), King and Queen County
byways.where: SR 14 from US 360 at St. Stephens Church through King and Queen Court House to SR 33 at Shacklefords

facts.fact: SR 14 here is The Trail, a winding road with many right-angle turns that is the main road of King and Queen County, passing Bruington, Stevensville, King and Queen Court House, Shanghai and Elsom.
Designated March 21, 2002, from SR 33 at Shacklefords to US 360 at St. Stephens Church.

byways.name: Mathews County byways
byways.where: SR 14 (New Point Comfort Highway) loop from Bavon through Port Haywood to Mathews, with Haven Beach, Bethel Beach, North River and East River roads

facts.fact: Designated April 20, 2000: a loop from Bavon through Port Haywood to Mathews on SR 14 and county roads to Haven Beach and Bethel Beach, plus North River Road and East River Road toward Mobjack.
New Point Comfort Light, finished in 1804 off the tip of the peninsula, is the third-oldest surviving light on the Chesapeake Bay.
The East River feeds into Mobjack Bay.

byways.name: Eastern Shore byways (Seaside Road and Wachapreague)
byways.where: SR 600 (Seaside Road) from US 13 at Kiptopeke through Nassawadox to Mappsburg; SR 603 Willis Wharf Road; SR 180 Pungoteague to Wachapreague; SR 605, US 13 Business, SR 126 and SR 179 through Accomac to Onancock

facts.fact: SR 600 (Seaside Road) from Kiptopeke to Exmore was designated February 17, 1994, with Nassawadox as a destination; the Accomack roads to Wachapreague and Onancock appear on the VDOT byways map.
SR 180 crosses the peninsula from Pungoteague Creek on the bay side through Keller to the waterfront at Wachapreague, on a channel in the seaside marshes.
The Wachapreague Channel winds through the seaside marsh to the barrier islands and reaches the Atlantic between Cedar and Parramore islands.
Onancock, on Onancock Creek, was founded in 1680.

byways.name: Green Sea Byway
byways.where: Sandpiper and Sandbridge roads, Indian River, Muddy Creek, Mill Landing and Morris Neck roads around Back Bay; Princess Anne, Pungo Ferry and Blackwater roads to the North Carolina line (City of Virginia Beach)

facts.fact: Designated January 16, 2003 as the Green Sea Byway: one branch circles Back Bay from the Back Bay National Wildlife Refuge by Sandbridge to Princess Anne Road at Creeds; the other runs Princess Anne, Pungo Ferry and Blackwater roads to the North Carolina line.

Back Bay is rimmed by loblolly pine, live oak and holly with bald cypress and cordgrass at its edges, with Pungo farmland to the west and Sandbridge to the east; Mill Landing is a public boat landing on the bay.
The Back Bay refuge was established in 1938 to protect wintering waterfowl, with 4.5 miles of dunes and beach.

byways.name: Route 72 (Dungannon Road / Hanging Rock Parkway), Coeburn to Dungannon
byways.where: SR 72 from Coeburn to Dungannon (Wise, Scott)

facts.fact: Designated March 9, 1995 from Coeburn to Dungannon, with Hanging Rock as a destination.
South of Coeburn SR 72 crosses the Guest River and Stone Mountain and follows the Clinch River to Dungannon.

byways.review: Listed as a Virginia Byway (from CTB minutes) but not present in the VDOT Byways_022024 layer; no agency line. Check whether VDOT still carries it.

byways.name: Route 46 (Christanna Highway), Brunswick County
byways.where: SR 46 from the North Carolina line near Bowens Corner through Lawrenceville to the Nottoway County line (Brunswick)

facts.fact: Designated November 18, 2004 from the North Carolina line to the Nottoway County line.
All of SR 46 in Brunswick County is a Virginia Byway; it passes Valentines, the remains of Fort Christanna and the county seat of Lawrenceville, and crosses the Nottoway River on the Kennedy Bridge.

byways.review: Listed as a Virginia Byway (from CTB minutes) but not present in the VDOT Byways_022024 layer; no agency line. Check whether VDOT still carries it.

byways.name: Route 903 (Goodes Ferry Road), Mecklenburg County
byways.where: SR 903 from US 58 in South Hill to the Brunswick County line near Joyceville (Mecklenburg)

facts.fact: Designated May 17, 2006 from US 58 in South Hill to the Brunswick County line near Joyceville, where it meets the Brunswick byway on Hendricks Mill Road.

byways.review: Listed as a Virginia Byway (from CTB minutes) but not present in the VDOT Byways_022024 layer; no agency line. Check whether VDOT still carries it.

byways.name: Big Walker Mountain Scenic Byway
byways.where: SR 717 and US 52 over Big Walker Mountain between I-77 exits near Wytheville and Bland (Wythe and Bland counties)

facts.fact: A 16-mile Forest Service byway (1989) around Big Walker Mountain, named for Dr. Thomas Walker, who came through in 1749.
The US 52 section leads to Big Walker Lookout, a 100-foot tower with a 360-degree view; Big Bend Picnic Area and Stony Fork camping are on the route.

byways.review: Its US 52 and SR 717 roads are also Virginia Byways (Bland and Wythe members).

byways.name: Highlands Scenic Byway
byways.where: Loop from Longdale Furnace on SR 770, SR 850 and forest road 447, Alleghany and Rockbridge counties

facts.fact: A 20-mile National Forest Scenic Byway through mixed forest past the remnants of a once thriving mining community.
Longdale Furnace keeps an 1827 stone furnace stack, the Longdale Iron Company office and laboratory, and two tall brick chimneys, listed as a historic district in 1998.

byways.review: The route description (SR 770, SR 850, FR 447) is from secondary sources; no live Forest Service page was found.

byways.name: Mount Rogers Scenic Byway
byways.where: SR 603 from Troutdale to Konnarock and US 58 from Damascus to Volney, Mount Rogers National Recreation Area

facts.fact: Designated in 1988; two sections, 13.2 miles of SR 603 from Troutdale to Konnarock and 32.5 miles of US 58 from Damascus to Volney, about 60 miles as a loop.
Damascus, where several long trails meet, is known as Trail Town USA and holds the annual Trail Days festival.
Mount Rogers, 5,729 feet, is the highest point in Virginia; the Appalachian Trail and the Virginia Creeper Trail cross the recreation area, and Grayson Highlands State Park adjoins it.

byways.review: US 58 Damascus to Konnarock and SR 603 are also Virginia Byways (Washington, Smyth and Grayson member).

issues: VDOT layer error: the US 58 designation requested by Patrick County (described as SR 8 north of Stuart to the Blue Ridge Parkway, LAD_SCEN_1 = 12) is drawn along US 58 from Damascus through Independence, Galax and Hillsville to Stuart, about 120 route miles. The member's gisWhere is restricted to RTE_FROM_M >= 221 (40 rows, route miles 221.9 to 235.5); confirm before drawing.

Catalog road trail-of-the-lonesome-pine-daniel-boone-heritage-trail-10300 merges two separate 1993 designations, and its line covers only the Daniel Boone Heritage Trail (US 23 / US 58, Weber City to Cumberland Gap). The member using that id is named Daniel Boone Heritage Trail; the Trail of the Lonesome Pine (US 19, SR 71, Alt US 58, SR 70, US 23 north, SR 160) has bywayId null and a gisWhere. Consider renaming the catalog entry.

Lee's Retreat: geomatch overlap between the catalog line (92 mapped miles) and the VDOT segments tagged Lee's Retreat is poor (only SR 600 near Rice matched at 1.0). The catalog line may follow the driving-tour route rather than the designated byway segments; consider replacing it with the VDOT segments (gisWhere on the member).

Virginia Coal Heritage Trail: the 2007 Act designates about 325 miles, but only segments newly designated by the Act carry the General Assembly tag in the VDOT layer; parts already designated in 1993 (Alt US 58, US 23, US 19) sit under the Trail of the Lonesome Pine member. The catalog coal line also overlaps the Lonesome Pine routes.

Byways named in the Wikipedia list (sourced to CTB minutes) but missing from the VDOT layer: SR 72 Coeburn to Dungannon (1995), SR 46 Christanna Highway in Brunswick (2004), SR 903 Goodes Ferry Road in Mecklenburg (2006) and Hendricks Mill Road in Brunswick, Union Mill Road (Fairfax SR 659), Old Colchester Road SR 825 (Fairfax), Stoney Point Road (Loudoun SR 719), and Fauquier SR 602, SR 623, SR 733 and SR 738. The first three are listed as members with no line; the rest are noted on their county members.

Designation dates and status uncertain for the Accomack County roads (SR 180, SR 605, US 13 Business, SR 126, SR 179) and Prince Edward SR 696: the VDOT route index gives 1994/1995 dates that do not appear in CTB minutes, and they appear unsigned, though they are on the VDOT map.
Aden Road: Wikipedia dates it July 11, 2017, but the CTB resolution and VDOT layer give December 7, 2016. The 2016 Prince William roads other than Aden Road are not yet in the Wikipedia list.

The VDOT page says the CTB has designated over 3,600 miles; the layer totals about 3,870 mapped miles, partly because divided highways are drawn in both directions and the US 58 error above. Shape__Length is in Web Mercator units and overstates length.

Mount Rogers and Big Walker Mountain National Forest Scenic Byways overlap Virginia Byway segments (Washington-Smyth-Grayson and Bland-Wythe members). They are listed under the Forest Service program with their catalog ids; the overlapping state members have bywayId null.

Highlands Scenic Byway: no live Forest Service page was found (fs.usda.gov URLs for the GWJ byways return 404); url points to the scenicbyways.info listing. Route description (SR 770, SR 850, FR 447) was only seen in secondary sources.
One VDOT row for SC-729N (Rappahannock County) has no description or date (about 6 mapped miles); it likely corresponds to Richmond Road, SR 729, designated February 19, 2014 per the Wikipedia list.
No official per-road pages exist for most Virginia Byways (the VDOT page names only the national routes); member url is null except for the national routes and the Virginia Coal Heritage Trail.
